target_customer: Originally ML engineers working on computer vision; now restaurant operators using vision AI on existing cameras
problem: Computer vision models fail in hidden ways and teams lacked tools to diagnose them; the company later applied its vision stack to restaurant operations such as drive-thru wait times and order accuracy.
product_category: Computer vision MLOps, later restaurant vision AI

founders.name: Botty Dimanov
education: PhD in Explainable AI for Vision, University of Cambridge (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page credits him with a US patent on extracting concepts from visual information.

founders.name: Dmitry Kazhdan
founders.background_notes: Named founder and CTO in the tech.eu seed article.

founders.name: Maleakhi Wijaya
founders.background_notes: tech.eu lists him among the founders as Founding Engineer.

competitors.name: Aquarium Learning
competitors.what: ML data operations platform to curate datasets and debug computer vision models
competitors.traction_then: Worked with computer vision companies; YC alumnus
competitors.funding_then: $2.6M seed led by Sequoia in February 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Diagnosing computer vision models and explaining failures builds on the founders' explainable AI research from Cambridge, which a small team could ship but rivals could not trivially copy.

defensibility.rationale: Early tooling for CV debugging faced well funded rivals and large labeling vendors; the restaurant product relies on integrations with existing cameras.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Adjacent tools expanded; Tenyks stayed independent and turned toward restaurant vision AI.

market_need_then: Computer vision deployments were growing in 2021 and teams complained about opaque model failures, a gap Aquarium also targeted.

branding.domain_note: Uses tenyks.ai; no acquisition story found.
branding.community_and_virality: Sponsors restaurant industry conferences; no community or merch evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: No documented brand story or press on the brand, and the invented name is unusual to spell.

pivots.from: MLOps monitoring and validation for computer vision engineers
pivots.to: Visual intelligence for restaurants using existing cameras
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; inferred from the 2022 seed article product description versus the current site, so cause is unknown.

outcome_analysis: Tenyks launched as a Cambridge spin-out debugging computer vision models, raised a $3.4M seed in March 2022 and by 2026 sells vision AI to restaurants, claiming 100+ customers including large chains. The cause of the shift away from MLOps is not public. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown report was found.
notes: Seed amount and investors from tech.eu, cross-checked by the Cambridge Enterprise and Business Weekly listings in search results. A separate $125k pre-seed in 2021 appears only on Seedtable and is unverified. Aquarium source is a search listing for the Medium post (not opened). Some outlets headline the seed as about human-AI interaction, which does not match the product description, so treat headline framing with care. Pivot is an inference, flagged as such. Brand origin unknown.
